title: Digital Passport for Artworks
summary: A browser-based prototype for issuing, verifying and revoking digital passports for artworks, with duplicate detection and human review routing, all client-side.

narrative.problem: An artwork's digital passport is only useful if the same work cannot be registered twice, even from a photo taken at a different angle, and if anyone can check that a passport was issued by a trusted authority and has not been altered or revoked.
narrative.decision: The whole lifecycle runs client-side in a single HTML file: fingerprints, similarity search, forgery-risk routing and a real ECDSA P-256 certificate chain via the Web Crypto API, with nothing leaving the browser tab except the optional MobileNet model.
narrative.tradeoff: With no server or database, there is no persistent registry: duplicate detection only compares submissions within one browser session, and refreshing the page clears all memory.
narrative.limitation: The README presents it as a prototype of the detection pipeline, not a production registry. The site notes that most forensic signals are hand-built heuristics kept as low-weight advisory signals, not a trained classifier.
narrative.caveat: Duplicate detection works within a single browser session only; refreshing the page clears all memory. Keys and certificates are generated in the browser for the demonstration.
